Two masses joined by a spring on a smooth surface oscillate at an angular frequency set by the spring constant and the reduced mass.
From the figure: $k = 150\ \text{N/m}$, $m_1 = 1\ \text{kg}$ and $m_2 = 200\ \text{g} = 0.2\ \text{kg}$.
Key concept: there is no external horizontal force, so the centre of mass stays at rest. The system behaves like a single body of reduced mass $\mu$ on the spring, with $\omega = \sqrt{k/\mu}$.
Reduced mass: $\mu = \dfrac{m_1 m_2}{m_1+m_2} = \dfrac{(1\ \text{kg})(0.2\ \text{kg})}{1.2\ \text{kg}} = \dfrac{1}{6}\ \text{kg}$
Substitute: $\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{150\ \text{N/m}}{1/6\ \text{kg}}} = \sqrt{900}\ \text{s}^{-1}$
So $\omega = 30\ \text{rad/s}$.
Answer: (C) 30
